scope: 16 whole-sentence scrambled-chunk tasks in four N4 structural families; 12 connected-text tasks in six original passages. Existing v1 choose/type model; no drag/drop, starred-position-only shortcut, timing system or exam-equivalence claim.

formatReferences.inspected: Composition of test items: sentential grammar 2 (sentence composition) and text grammar are distinct item types. HTML table extraction loses some image-based level headers; no timing or exact exam-item-count claim is derived.
Official page states that samples show item forms, one sample per type, and can differ from actual booklets. Used as a format reference only; no official question text copied.

inspectedPassages.use: Reported positive/negative instructions. Active 言う is not inherently passive; giver/addressee and contextual force remain distinct.
An embedded whether-question, not an assertion. Do not require douka in all unrestricted polar questions or infer scope from one adverb without context.
Bunpro #181 JLPT4: nonpast verb phrase modifies the planned-event noun. Past outer copula recalls a plan without implying failure. No mandatory booking or inverted modification claim.
Receiving viewpoint; the receiver and performer remain distinct under potential negation.
An existing purposeful result, including one produced by another person or superseded by a changed plan.

Preparatory action, with contextual timing. Not universally future: past preparation and retained-state uses exist. These tasks compare the printed nonpast future commitment with a stated existing result, not every possible use.
An action is not required; this is not a prohibition. Unrestricted synonyms exist outside the printed response contract.
A required action. The fictional passage states the applicable rule; no fixed external/internal-duty distinction is imposed.

levelPolicy: Bunpro-first N4 whole-operation mappings are reused from the named ledgers. Ordinary temporal attachment and case markers alone are not claimed to become N4; these tasks assemble complete reported/benefactive/modal/embedded-question structures or interpret N4 obligations and preparatory-result reports across context.
preflightCorrection: Discarded unpublished decision/intention prototypes after reading the existing ledger: ordinary ことにする is primary N3, and ordinary つもり alone would not establish this N4 ordering scope. All four plan tasks now assemble #181 予定 with prospective versus recalled-plan contexts; no old published level or task changed.
finiteOrderContract: Each accepted response is an exact concatenation of all printed chunks, each once, under the visible role/scope and final-predicate constraints. Nominal-phrase and embedded-question fronting alternatives are enumerated; no blanket single Japanese word-order rule.
responseClasses: Classes identify meaningful instruction/receiving participants or the A/B action under the modal/question scope. Both classes are correctly targeted in each family; no always-wrong distractor class or fake class mapping is introduced.
coverageLimits: Ordering has four tasks per existing structural family and two keys per role/scope facet. This bounded composition practice is not a new claim of deep mastery of each grammar usage. Each pair of text questions shares one passage key, with three passage keys per text facet.
nativePrerequisite: Neutral Android instructions from be7286c44ab598287cd9ce648356a7f320fdff86; final selected-pool instrumentation and real MainActivity rotation were completed separately from editorial review.

native.scope: Each set's selected pool in both themes, including wrong/correct choose/type, normalized responses, scroll to Check, full answer flow and article Back. Not every item in every mode.
